name: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid

criteria.description: Chronic blistering predominantly involving mucous membranes with scarring
Linear deposition of IgG, IgA, or C3 along the epithelial basement membrane zone on direct immunofluorescence
Histopathology showing subepidermal blister with inflammatory infiltrate
Detection of circulating autoantibodies against basement membrane zone antigens (BP180, BP230, laminin 332)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical mucosal blistering with scarring plus positive direct immunofluorescence findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires correlation of clinical, histopathological, and immunopathological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic mucosal blistering with subsequent scarring
pathognomonic.notes: Primarily affects oral, ocular, nasal, pharyngeal, laryngeal, and genital mucosa
searchTerms: long-lasting mouth or nose blisters that scar
chronic mucous membrane sores with scarring
repeated blistering and scarring of mucous lining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ocular conjunctival fibrosis and symblepharon formation
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to potential vision loss if untreated
searchTerms: eye lining scarring and eyelid sticking
fibrosis of conjunctiva causing eyelid adhesion
scar tissue forming in eye surface
blisters forming under outer skin layer

common.symptomName: Painful erosions and ulcerations of oral mucosa
common.notes: Leads to difficulty eating and oral discomfort

common.symptomName: Hoarseness or dysphonia from laryngeal involvement
searchTerms: hoarse or weak voice from throat involvement
voice changes due to larynx problems
tracheal narrowing leading to breathing problems

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss secondary to painful mucosal lesions
searchTerms: weight loss due to painful mouth sores
losing weight from painful mucosal lesions

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infections of mucosal erosions
searchTerms: secondary infections of mouth or skin ulcers
breathing tube placement due to obstruction

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: low red blood cells from bleeding
eye surface sores leading to blindness
damage to cornea with vision impairment

laboratory: Direct immunofluorescence showing linear IgG, IgA, or C3 deposition at basement membrane zone
Serologic detection of circulating autoantibodies against BP180, BP230, or laminin 332
imaging: Endoscopic visualization of mucosal erosions and strictures in esophagus or airway
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; autoimmune etiology
other: Histopathology revealing subepidermal blister with inflammatory infiltrate
Clinical evidence of mucosal scarring and fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly oral mucosal erosions without scarring
Predominantly cutaneous blistering with rare mucosal involvement
Less scarring compared to mucous membrane pemphigoid

redFlags: Progressive ocular scarring leading to vision loss
Airway obstruction due to laryngeal or tracheal involvement
Severe dysphagia causing malnutrition or aspiration risk
references: Chan LS, Ahmed AR, Anhalt GJ, et al. The first international consensus on mucous membrane pemphigoid: definition, diagnostic criteria, pathogenic factors, medical treatment, and prognostic indicators. Arch Dermatol. 2002;138(3):370-379.
Schmidt E, Zillikens D. Pemphigoid diseases. Lancet. 2013;381(9863):320-332.
Scully C, Porter SR. Oral mucous membrane pemphigoid: clinical features and management. Oral Dis. 2008;14(7):620-627.
